text: Welcome to Webb Cubing Club. Bring your cube, and a little curiosity. This is your place to learn with the club, practice at home, and take one small step at a time.
You do not need an account. Start with a short lesson. Speed can come later.
Choose Find my starting point. Four short questions suggest a learning route based on what you can already do, your goals, and how you practice.
This is not a test. If you cannot solve independently yet, the beginner's layer by layer route is a good place to start.
Read the reasons, then choose Start lesson. You can skip the questions, choose a route yourself, or change it later.
First, meet the moves. Hold white on top and green in front. U means up, D down, L left, R right, F front, and B back.
A plain letter is a clockwise quarter turn, looking straight at that face. A prime means counterclockwise. A two means a half turn.
Choose U prime, then Direction view. Press Play and copy the upper layer on your cube. Replay slowly if you need. Moving the camera only changes your view.
In Learn, begin with the holding and notation introduction. Follow the club leader's lesson in a meeting, or work through the stages at your own pace.
For the first cross, build white petals around the yellow center. Match each petal's side color to its center, then turn it down.
To copy this exact example, open Follow along with a physical cube. Apply its scramble from solved, with white up and green front. Our screen is already prepared.
Use Next move to watch one turn. Read the goal and result check. A stage jump changes only the screen; follow all earlier moves on your real cube.
Later, explore the algorithm library and formula practice. Learn to recognize a case before revealing its answer. Beginner and Advanced C F O P are there when you are ready.
Stuck with a cube in your hands? Open Solve your cube. Choose your method. If you know the scramble, paste it and ask for an explained solution.
This short example has already been prepared. Follow its verified stages with the same player. Keep your cube's holding aligned, including any shown whole cube rotations.
Or choose Enter colors. Copy all six faces using each holding diagram. Review them, then Check colors. Fix any errors before generating a solution.
When you can solve independently, try Timer. Apply the random scramble from solved. Compare the six face diagram to check your cube before you begin.
On a keyboard, hold Space until Ready, then release to start. Press Space again to stop. This is a short control demonstration, not a real solve.
On a touch screen, hold the large timer until Ready, release, then touch it again to stop. Optional inspection gives you time to look before starting.
The history here uses labeled example results. See individual times, averages of five and twelve, and the trend. You can correct a result with plus two or D N F.
Records stay in this browser, on this device. Export C S V or J S O N before clearing browser data or changing devices. There is no automatic cloud sync.
Need a reminder? Open Guide for screenshots and written instructions. Expand Every control, explained for the details. Page tours show the controls right where you use them.
You can skip a step or exit a tour at any time. For today, learn one unfamiliar move, try one lesson, and repeat it with your cube.
Come back for another small step tomorrow. Learn it here. Try it in your hands. Your turn.
